questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How parents should teach babies to read
Why some babies start talking late
The skills babies need to develop in order to speak
How adults learn a second language
questions.why: They discover how babies learn to speak and hear the skills babies develop.

questions.q: What do Georgie and Phil think babies do to learn to speak?
options: They learn from watching TV
They watch and copy adults, and Phil saw his children do this
They learn mostly from other babies and older brothers and sisters
They start with long sentences
questions.why: Georgie imagines they copy adults, and Phil says that's what his children did.

questions.q: According to Professor Julian Pine, what is one of the first things a child must do?
options: Learn the alphabet
Copy their parents' accent and the way they speak
Learn to make long sounds
Break the stream of speech into separate words
questions.why: He says the child has got to break down the speech stream into words.

questions.q: What helps babies find where English words begin?
options: English words often start with a stressed syllable
English words always end with a vowel, which makes them easier
Adults speak very slowly to babies
English words are usually very short
questions.why: Phil says in English, words often begin with a stressed syllable.

questions.q: Why do small children sometimes call a giraffe a 'raffe'?
options: They leave out the first syllable because it isn't stressed
They can't say the letter 'g' until they are about five years old
They are copying a cartoon
They think it's a funny word
questions.why: Pine says children leave off the unstressed syllable, which is not typical English.

questions.q: What example does presenter Michael Rosen give from his own family?
options: His daughter said 'nana' for grandmother
His son couldn't say 'banana'
He called his son 'my sminge'
His son called a machine a 'sminge'
questions.why: He says his son used to call a machine a 'sminge'.

questions.q: What is the second skill babies need, according to Professor Pine?
options: Making their mouths and tongues move faster
Speaking in full sentences
Linking words to the things they refer to
Recognising different voices
questions.why: He says they've got to link words to things in the environment and learn what words mean.

questions.q: Why does Professor Pine mention a cup and a pen?
options: To show which words babies learn first
To show how hard it is for a child to know which object a word means
To describe a simple test he gives to young children in his laboratory
To explain why babies like objects
questions.why: He asks how a child knows you mean the cup or the pen, because the speech signal is ambiguous.
